title: Microsoft Edge: Enhanced Autofill adds passports and driver's licences on desktop
summary: Hold: the guidance mistakes a site blocklist for an allowlist and omits that AutofillSettings does not apply to profiles signed in with a personal Microsoft account. The policy path and registry reference are correct, but the statements that its applicability and autofill sync are undocumented also need correction.

claims.where: What's changing; Open questions: saved documents and sync
claims.claim: Where saved autofill documents are stored and whether they roam remains an undocumented question.
claims.quote: If you're signed in and syncing, your autofill data is synced across all versions of Microsoft Edge where you're signed in with the same credentials. When syncing, all autofill data is stored on encrypted Microsoft servers.
claims.fix: Replace the storage/sync gap with: 'Microsoft's privacy page states that, when signed in and syncing, autofill data syncs across Edge versions signed in with the same credentials, and all autofill data is stored on encrypted Microsoft servers when syncing.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/legal/microsoft-edge/privacy#autofill. Narrow the open question to 'Where are identity documents stored locally?'

It does not apply to profiles signed in with a personal Microsoft account.' Keep the separate testing advice.

claims.claim: Replacing * with narrower URL patterns allows identity documents on named sites only.

Setting this policy allows you to specify which AutoFill data types are blocked on specific URL patterns.

claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'Use narrower URL patterns instead of "*" to block identity documents only on matching sites; sites that match no entry remain unblocked by this policy. Blocked types from multiple matching entries are combined.' Do not describe these patterns as an allowlist.
